However, our boys packed splendidly, which is the main thing to remember in cross-country running, and with Harry Greene 10th, J.

He was well supported by Harry Greene but Adams and Simpson did not do so well as they did in the Southern race. However, our team position of seventh was very good and a big improvement on previous results.

The team of Belgrave Policemen who won the M.P.A.A. 10 Miles Team Championship—Sapcote, Evans, McGreechan and Atkinson. Harry Greene 1st in the Inter Schools race for the Densham Cup. Ken England and Jim Kennedy on their recent marriages.

On the first leg we had Harry Greene running for us and he ran a fine race to give the Bels the lead. Harry is now developing a good judgment of pace and also of when to time his effort and should be well to the fore next season over the country.
The 880 yds. saw Brian Rice making a welcome appearance in our colours and with Harry Greene they managed to finish 3rd and 4th, although we actually had two non-scorers in Doug.
Harry Greene, after doing most of the pace-making, finished 3rd in the 1 mile and it is evident that we have some very promising material in the ranks of our younger members.

Harry Greene, although short of training, ran well to finish ninth, and with Peter Courtney scoring eleventh, we thus won the team race with a score of 24 points, with Herne Hill H. scoring 40 and the Wallington County School 41.

Goode, our Youths champion, had been in bed during the week with 'flu and he should not really have run but did not want to let the team down. Harry Greene ran the race of his life to finish in 5th place with Brian Trower 31st, Peter Courtney 40th and H.

The Youths event saw the club nearest to gaining a place, and our lads were unlucky in losing third team awards by the narrow margin of six points. Harry Greene again ran well and was well backed up by Peter Courtney and Geoff Goode. Brian Trower ran below his Southern form but H.

On the same day at the Ilford Youths' Road Relay our youngsters put up a very fine show by winning this event and beating the Southern Youth Champions, Southgate Harriers, into second place. Harry Greene gave us the lead on the first stage and this was held by F.
Harry Greene could only finish fourth in the one mile, but our junior medley relay team of Rodgers, A.
Rodgers second, and Geoff Goode won the 1 mile, with Harry Greene in second place. Our team also won the junior 4 x 110 yards relay, and it would take a very good club side to beat our boys.

Frank Kemp won the junior 100 and was second in the furlong, and Peter Hunt finished second in the quarter, with Gerry Trower in a similar position in the half-mile. Harry Greene was fourth in the mile, but we won the long jump, with A.
Wise; 2, H.

The 1 mile (under 19) event saw the limit man retain his lead throughout, with Harry Greene making a good effort to overtake him. Peter Courtney was third and Don Maclean, who was the scratch man, seemed to be having a training run only.
We hope that they will be able to secure leave to run for us during the coming track season, but Harry Greene is not so fortunate as he is now in Benghazi.
